teaser: An answer to Ralf Thomas: the shell game works because nothing is written down, and a behaviour policy's explicit prohibitions move the liability line.
core_idea: Agent vendors can deflect accountability because nothing written stands between a customer's allow and the failure; an Agent Behaviour Policy's explicit prohibitions, still mostly hope, become the evidence that moves liability between deployer and vendor when broken, so every agent in a loop should take a policy beside its prompt and its vendor should honour and report against it.

nodes.label: Ralf Thomas's post
nodes.summary: If an employee wrecks a client's systems the company pays; why should AI agents be different?

nodes.label: The shell game
nodes.summary: Blame the agent, blame the customer, hide behind the contract, disclose late.

nodes.label: The 2026 record
nodes.summary: Deleted files, an escape to Hugging Face, real systems reached in evaluations, an outage called user error.

nodes.label: Stated more carefully
nodes.summary: The cases were early rulings, the Air Canada phrase is the tribunal's, the Copilot line is gone; the pattern survives.

nodes.label: Nothing written down
nodes.summary: Between allow and the failure there is reach and a prompt, and no statement of what the agent must not do.

nodes.label: Agent Behaviour Policy
nodes.summary: The mandate written down beside the measured reach, with explicit prohibitions.

nodes.label: Explicit prohibitions
nodes.summary: Do not send, do not start scheduled tasks, do not attack other sites, speak on your own behalf, make no offers.

nodes.label: Still mostly hope
nodes.summary: A written rule kept by the model and enforced by nobody: an expectation, but on the record.

nodes.label: Liability shifts to the platform
nodes.summary: A prohibition the agent breaks turns you allowed it into the product ignored what it was told.

nodes.label: Towards the world, the deployer
nodes.summary: Customers and regulators deal with the deployer; the moment of authorisation is the grant.

nodes.label: Software as a product
nodes.summary: The EU product liability rules apply from 9 December 2026; the Bundestag passed Germany's version on 8 October.

nodes.label: A policy beside every prompt
nodes.summary: Every agent in a loop, anything with the lethal trifecta, takes a behaviour policy as a separate input.

nodes.label: The vendor's half
nodes.summary: Accept the policy, honour it, enforce what the platform can see, report every breach and near miss.

nodes.label: Will vendors accept it?
nodes.summary: Whether platforms will take business rules as an input and answer for them.

quotes.text: The shell game works because nothing was written down.
quotes.why: The diagnosis the post's four moves share.

quotes.text: It is about whether the product did what it was explicitly told.
quotes.why: Where the written policy moves the dispute.

figures.caption: The four moves of the accountability shell game, from Ralf Thomas's post, and what a written policy changes in each.
Two directions of liability: towards the world, and between the deployer and the vendor, decided by the written policy.
